meta.sourceAsar: npm registry: 39 x @deepseek-ai/*@0.2.2-rc.5 packages (lib/typert.remote-client.js each; no desktop build exists for this tag)
meta.crossCheckTree: npm-published rc.5 packages (subset of the desktop runtime package set)

layers.A_sdk_jsonrpc: Explicit documented wire protocol (README) — external client / forwarder path.
layers.B_typert_remote: Host<->Client Remote endpoints; JSON Schemas recovered from generated lib/typert.remote-client.js (39 packages / 224 endpoints, 0 extraction errors).
layers.C_cordis_ctx: In-process Cordis ctx.* service surface — TYPED/SOURCED from the official repo TypeScript at tag dsh-v0.2.2-rc.5, cross-checked against the npm-published rc.5 packages compiled .js (151 production keys / 1367 methods / 80 cross-check-confirmed).

meta.honesty: Layer B schemas are exact (generated from the Host FaceModel). Layer A payload field shapes are transcribed from the protocol README because TS types are erased in shipped .js. Layer C is typed/sourced from the official repo .ts at the locked tag (NOT reverse-engineered): npm ships no .ts source and the same-package .d.ts is absent from the shipped packages, so each key's provider type is read from the public TypeScript and the runtime registration is cross-checked against the shipped .js (npm-published rc.5 packages, a subset of the desktop package set, so fewer keys confirm).

transport.framing: one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per '\n'-terminated line over caller-owned byte streams
transport.dispatch: id+method=request; id alone=response; method alone=notification; malformed lines ignored
transport.lifecycle: start() attaches stream listeners; close() detaches them and rejects pending requests without destroying the streams

methods: Handshake. approvalRequests:true enables approval/request; capabilities.userQuestions:true enables user-question/ask; reasoningEffort optional non-empty adapter id; maxTokens optional positive safe int; resolves the exact provider/model route and rejects session/prompt until handshake succeeds. serverInfo.name is wire-stable 'deepseek-harness-sdk-runtime'; serverInfo.version is '0.0.1' (unvalidated).

Queues content blocks without native slash-command routing (runtime skill recognition still applies). SessionPromptResult.messageId = the queued user message id (a durable enqueue receipt, not a model result).

Accepts {sessionId, contentBlocks: SdkPromptContentBlock[]}. Returns {kind:'prompt', messageId} for queued ordinary input, or {kind:'command', execution} after a supported command settles. A command requires one complete text block plus only encoded images; empty/all-blank text rejected; image-only allowed; strings normalize to a text block.

Accepts non-empty persisted {sessionId}; restores that exact session (requires initialization + the original persistence store). Sends no new input; rejects missing/unreadable/incompatible/occupied sessions without creating a replacement.
Accepts {sessionId}; returns {} after the root stays idle and progressing managed descendant work finishes; unknown ids and live Agent failures without a newer committed terminal are rejected.

OPT-IN: requires InitializeParams.approvalRequests == true. Params {sessionId, toolName, callId?, reason?}; Result {outcome: 'allowed-once' | 'rejected' | 'cancelled'}. Only 'allowed-once' grants exactly one operation. Cancellation discards the pending request and late responses; shutdown/transport loss fail decisions closed.

OPT-IN: requires InitializeParams.capabilities.userQuestions == true. Params {requestId, sessionId, questions}; Result {answers:[{id, selected, custom?}]} naming every question id exactly once, OR {cancelled:true} (dismissal -> native ASK_CANCELLED). Invalid batches -> BAD_ANSWER; host/transport failures -> PROVIDER_ERROR.
Identifies the request that stopped waiting; host cancels its own work and discards the question.
Every session event in the runtime, unfiltered.
Sent for the same commandId after a command query's model activity starts / state-only commands need no model turn.
Subagent finished (in-process runs only). lastAssistantMessage = child's last non-empty assistant message, or accumulated assistant text; absent when neither exists.

payloadTypes.InitializeParams: { approvalRequests?: boolean; capabilities?: { userQuestions?: boolean }; reasoningEffort?: string (non-empty adapter-owned id); maxTokens?: positive safe int }
payloadTypes.SdkUserQuestionResult: { answers: [{ id, selected, custom? }] } | { cancelled: true }
payloadTypes.SdkPromptContentBlock: ordinary durable content + SdkEncodedImageBlock { type: 'image', data, mimeType } (server converts encoded images to durable refs before enqueue)
payloadTypes._note: TypeScript types are erased in shipped .js; these shapes are transcribed verbatim from dsh-sdk-protocol/README.md (Payload semantics). Notification payloads depend on SessionEvent (dsh-session), ContentBlock (dsh-llm), SubagentStopReason (dsh-subagent).

knownLimitations: No protocol-version negotiation (handshake carries only serverInfo.version = '0.0.1', unvalidated).
No cancel or session-close methods; a client abandons a turn by closing the runtime process.
Question waits are process-local; question request ids are not durable handles across a runtime restart.

endpoints.description: Kill one background job on a human's behalf. The request's session is the fenced read's caller, so the job must be one that session can see: the registry's owner fence is the only access rule, and a child session's own jobs are killable from its list like any other. The kill records `cancelled by the user` as its reason; it is not one the model requested, so the owning agent still receives the completion notice, and a shell tool waiting on that job reads the reason in its own result.

endpoints.description: Parse and execute a known command without sending it to the model. A resolved command's lifecycle is logged: `command/run` is appended before the handler is invoked and `command/done` after settlement (a thrown or aborted handler settles as `kind: 'error'`). Both are direct log-only appends — no turn wraps them, and persistence drains them at ordinary checkpoints. Admission misses (syntax or unknown name) log nothing — they never entered a handler. A `command/run` append failure fails the execution loud; a `command/done` append failure on the handler-failure path is contained so the handler's own error stays the reported failure. Attachment admission is enforced here, not in the composer: attachments sent to a command that does not declare `input.attachments`, an absent attachment store, and an exceeded image limit each settle as an error result before the handler runs. Validation rejection starts no attachment writes; a storage failure can leave only unreachable content-addressed objects for deferred collection.

GitHub repositories get a connection check bounded by githubConnectionTimeoutMs before pnpm starts; only network failures or timeouts stop installation, and a stop streams the check's diagnostic as the installation's install-log run under its request id, while pnpm owns authentication and transport fallback. An HTTP(S) Git URL on another host is installed over SSH instead when access probes bounded by gitTransportTimeoutMs find that only SSH can read it. endpoints.description: Replace an installed bundle with a newer version. A registry copy updates to `name@version`, checked on the registry first: it must exist, declare a bundle, and accept the running DSH version, or nothing changes. A Git copy updates to the Git spec `options.spec` names, which must pin a full commit of the repository directory the copy came from; with HMR, a network failure or timeout reaching its repository stops the update before anything changes. pnpm reads a Git package only while installing it, so its bundle and compatibility are checked then. Either target installation is undone, profile files and modules included, before its bundle loads unless it installs `name` at `version`. With HMR the installed version is removed, so its plugins stop, and the target is installed with the same selection; when that installation fails or is cancelled, the removed version is installed again: a registry copy from the registry it came from, a Git copy from its saved spec. Without HMR the target is installed over the running version and the result reports the restart.

parameters.description: Installed profile dependency name.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Exact version newer than the installed one.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: The registry asked first, as for `listVersions`; the Git spec of `version`, required for and accepted only by a bundle `listBundles` lists with `update: 'git'`; and the request id naming the progress and the target installation's logs and cancellation.

spec.description: The Git spec of the target version: required for a bundle listed with `update: 'git'`, where it must pin a full commit of the installed copy's repository directory, and refused for any other.

requestId.description: Names the update's progress and the target installation's logs; `cancelInstall` stops only that installation.

endpoints.description: Delete every ended Host task, leaving active tasks armed. Ended tasks never schedule another delivery, so the removal changes no pending target and no timer is recomputed. Rows are enumerated and removed in one FIFO slot, so a delivery ordered behind this call ends its task after the enumeration rather than during it. The batch is one domain write: a normal failure rejects with every listed row still stored, while a backend `unknown-state` failure may have removed rows and quarantines the Host domain, so later schedule operations reject until the domain is reopened. A successful nonempty batch emits `schedule/changed` without Agent notices. A rejected batch announces `schedule/changed` because it does not establish which rows landed, and clients then re-read the catalog.

result.description: Count of removed rows; zero when the Host held no ended task.

deleted.description: Ended task rows this call removed; zero when the Host held none.

The request requires an open turn because the audit pair must be enclosed by the durable log's commit/replay boundary; an idle ask rejects before appending anything. The answerer phase always produces an outcome: an aborted signal yields `'cancelled'`, a missing or throwing answerer yields `'unavailable'` (fail closed), and a rogue non-vocabulary return value is normalized to `'unavailable'`. A failure that prevents either audit append from committing still rejects because returning an unlogged decision would violate the pair. Session contains post-commit observer failures, so an authoritative append cannot reject the request or suppress its matching audit event. append commit point.

methods.doc: Return path metadata without following the final path component when it is a symbolic link. This is intentionally path-shaped, not target-shaped: {@link resolve} follows symlinks to produce the stable identity used by normal reads/writes, while `lstat` lets a consumer reject the path itself before that follow happens. `opts.cwd` follows {@link resolve}'s cwd rules. `undefined` means the path is absent.

methods.doc: Stream the whole regular text file as decoded text chunks (same text semantics as {@link readText}, for large files). The backend owns cross-chunk UTF-8 decoding and binary rejection so the policy layer never touches raw bytes.

methods.name: readBytes
methods.signature: abstract readBytes(target: FsTarget, signal: AbortSignal | undefined, maxBytes: number): Promise<Uint8Array>
methods.doc: Read the whole regular file as raw bytes with no decoding or binary rejection. The bound lives at this seam so a backend can never buffer an unbounded file: a target known or discovered to exceed `maxBytes` fails with `FS_TOO_LARGE` instead of returning a truncated result.

methods.name: readByteRange
methods.signature: abstract readByteRange(target: FsTarget, range: { offset: number; length: number }, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Uint8Array>
methods.doc: Read one byte window of the regular file as raw bytes with no decoding or binary rejection: the bytes at `[offset, offset + length)`, shorter when the file ends inside the window and empty when `offset` lies at or past its end. The window is the bound here, not the file: a backend transfers at most `length` bytes of content beyond the prefix it skips to reach `offset` and never buffers the whole file, so the caller's cap on `length` is the guard against unbounded buffering.

methods.doc: Atomically create or replace UTF-8 text. `expected` guards intent and staleness; omission allows unconditional overwrite. runs under; a sandboxing backend fences the write by it, the bare backend ignores it. Omit to leave the backend its own default.

When supplied, the version guard is checked before matching so stale content reports `FS_STALE_VERSION`; omission edits the current content without a freshness precondition. under; a sandboxing backend fences the edit by it, the bare backend ignores it. Omit to leave the backend its own default.

methods.name: patchText

methods.doc: Atomically apply parsed hunks to the LF-normalized text and restore the stored line-ending style. A missing or stale target reports `FS_STALE_VERSION`; an unmatched hunk reports `FS_PATCH_MISMATCH`. under; a sandboxing backend fences the patch by it, the bare backend ignores it. Omit to leave the backend its own default.

methods.name: deleteFile
methods.signature: abstract deleteFile( target: FsTarget, expected?: { version: FsVersion }, signal?: AbortSignal, sandboxPolicy?: SandboxExecutionPolicy, ): Promise<FsDeleteOutcome>
methods.doc: Remove a regular file. A missing or stale target reports `FS_STALE_VERSION`; a directory or other non-file reports `FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE`. Resolution has already followed symlinks, so the target is the real file. runs under; a sandboxing backend fences it, the bare backend ignores it. Omit to leave the backend its own default.

methods.name: moveFile
methods.signature: abstract moveFile( source: FsTarget, destination: FsTarget, options: { hunks?: readonly PatchHunk[] expectedSource?: { version: FsVersion } expectedDestination?: FsWriteIntent }, signal?: AbortSignal, sandboxPolicy?: SandboxExecutionPolicy, ): Promise<FsMoveOutcome>
methods.doc: Publish the source text, optionally patched, at the destination, then remove the source. Both targets stay locked in canonical order. Identical targets report `FS_SAME_TARGET`; the source guard follows `patchText` and the destination guard follows `writeText`. The two effects are separate: a published destination with a retained source is a final outcome reported through `sourceDeleted: false`. under; a sandboxing backend fences them, the bare backend ignores it. Omit to leave the backend its own default.

Every `val` is a DETACHED structured clone — never the live cell reference: the watermark cache is this registry's authoritative mutable state, and a caller reaching the live reference could corrupt every subsequent snapshot and frame through it (plain JSON by the unit contract, so the clone is total). A released unit contributes the Session's last cell. The registry no longer advances that cell, while a retained handle read still advances it forward, so a writer running after a plugin unloads keeps that unit's latest state; a Session that has no cell of it gets no row. {@link restore} folds only live units, so its refreshed rows omit released units.

The one-below anchor is load-bearing: the tail then proves how far the stored log still extends, so {@link restore} can detect a log that shrank below a row's watermark (crash-repair truncation) instead of serving the stale row as current — an empty tail read from the anchor yields an end below every watermark and the restore rejects for a full re-read. or `undefined` when no live unit is registered (released predecessors do not count; no read needed — {@link restore} would serve empty values regardless).

A row is usable iff its `ver` matches the live unit's `stateVersion`, it does not predate `baseSeq` (`seq >= baseSeq - 1`), and it does not claim events past the supplied end (`seq <= endSeq`); an unusable row is discarded and its key refolds from `init` — which is only sound over the full log, so a discarded row with `baseSeq > 0` throws (the caller re-reads from seq 0, e.g. after a crash-repair truncation shrank the log below a row's watermark). supplied event's seq, `baseSeq - 1` for an empty tail) plus the refreshed checkpoint rows at that cut, ready for a durable write-back. methods.name: projectedLabels
methods.signature: private projectedLabels<T extends { readonly record: SessionRecord }>( items: readonly T[], ): Array<T &
methods.doc: The mention label and display title each listed Session's projections can answer without reading its log. Attachment is decided by the store at read time, not by the listing: a session that attached in between would otherwise be answered from a checkpoint its live log has already moved past. An attached session answers from its live registry cut, which advances with every committed event, so a rename or a just-generated title is visible immediately; its events are already in memory, so the lazy fold costs no I/O. A cold session answers from the durable checkpoint the projection cache wrote when it went cold. Nothing else is attempted. Folding a title from a log costs the whole log, and this call sits under every keystroke of `@` completion. A session that no projection can answer for — one persisted before the cache was composed — is labeled by its id and cannot be found by its title until it is opened once, which checkpoints it. Services are resolved once per call and the cache's snapshot method is bound once: a service lookup per listed session would dominate the call.
